original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact subspace-cut cone for the fixed S4 mixed tuple. Arbitrary natural four-dimensional subspaces over every field obey the inequality; valid binary-word cuts use characteristic two. All 2,825 subspaces of the binary six-dimensional unordered-pair module are separately enumerated. Each cut acts on one module copy, uniformly over scalar roles.
scope_change_reason: Take PR2998 explicit arbitrary-subspace successor. This broadens its proof-method class instead of repeating a word census or assuming coordinate cuts exhaust linear cuts.
bottleneck_link: A sharper paid-call invariant could close the 20 versus 21 mixed-target gap. This scoped obstruction proves these natural and edge subspace cuts cannot provide it. It supplies no native bit supplier.
stop_rule: Finish one exact cone certificate and its source-bound independent replay. Stop before coupled-copy/larger-module searches, word synthesis or supplier adoption.
evidence: PROOF.md; RESULT.json complete binary inventories and shared duals; code-disjoint RREF/rank replay over F2 plus finite F3/F5 natural controls; actual optimized CLI mutants.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used in preparation and checking. The two implementations were prepared in one session; no independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a coupled-copy subspace or a larger representation improve the mixed-tuple cut bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The enlarged one-copy natural and edge cone remains 20 while direct scalar words cost 21.
open_questions.first_step: Specify a characteristic-two module, one actual subspace and all three generator cuts. Test whether its tuple cut exceeds four times the sum of its generator cuts.
open_questions.blocked_by: No stronger valid cut or complete word is supplied; the present finite theorem does not cover coupled copies or larger modules.

open_questions.question: Does the actual arbitrary-dirty-role circuit cost 20 or 21?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cut-method optimum is not the circuit optimum.
open_questions.first_step: Analyze equality in the inherited ordered-pair bound or exhibit a full formal word with twelve letters and eight exterior letters.
open_questions.blocked_by: A word or stronger invariant and complete physical supplier obligations remain absent.
